pages.chapter: The Fox That Was Not a Fox
pages.text: Toby sat in the backyard. He was thinking. Next to him, a cup hung in the air. It did not bob or drift. It just hung there, as still as a rock. Toby did not see it.
pages.picture: Toby sitting on the lawn of Julia's backyard, eyes half closed, deep in thought; beside him a tin cup hangs in mid-air about two feet up, perfectly still; Toby hasn't noticed it; calm warm afternoon

pages.text: Julia sat on the back step with her snack. Then the grass at the gate shook. A fox slid under the gate! It ran up, took her snack, and dashed off.
pages.picture: Julia on the back step of the house holding a bowl of crackers; a fox slipping under the wooden garden gate and snatching a cracker from her bowl; Julia surprised

pages.text: "Stop!" said Julia. "That is my snack!" The fox froze and looked back at her. In the sun, its fur shone pink and green and blue. Just like Toby's scales.
pages.picture: the fox frozen in the middle of the lawn with the snack in its mouth, looking back over its shoulder; its red fur glints with pink, green and blue in the sunlight; Julia pointing, Toby behind her staring

pages.text: Then a boy jumped down from the next yard. It was Max. He did not stop to think. "I will get it!" he yelled. He ran after the fox and did not look. Bang! He ran smack into Toby.
pages.picture: Max, a bold eight-year-old boy, has leapt down from the neighbour's fence and is running flat out across the lawn after the fox, about to crash into Toby's side

pages.text: Toby got a big fright. Whoosh! Max shot up, up, up, as high as the treetops! Then he drifted down, as soft as a leaf.
pages.picture: Max high in the air at the height of the treetops above the backyard, arms and legs spread, amazed; Toby below, startled and wide-eyed; Julia with hands on her cheeks

pages.text: Max landed on the grass. He looked at Toby. Toby looked at Max. Julia held still. "Again!" said Max. "Do it again!"
pages.picture: Max sitting on the grass grinning up at Toby, arms raised; Toby shy and unsure; Julia standing between them, holding her breath

pages.text: Julia held his hand. "Max, can you keep this hush-hush?" "Yes! But the fox!" said Max. The fox was a speck of pink and green at the end of the backyard. Then it was in the woods.
pages.picture: Julia holding Max's hand, finger to her lips, serious; Max pointing past her at the far end of the backyard where the shimmering fox slips through the back gate into the woods

pages.text: They ran after it. Max shot up a tree to look. Toby zoomed past the ferns. Julia bent down to look for tracks in the mud. "There!" said Julia. "It went to the pond!"
pages.picture: in the woods: Max high up in a tree, looking out; Toby flying close above the ferns; Julia crouching by small paw prints in the mud, pointing ahead toward the pond

pages.text: The fox was stuck at the pond. It had no way out. Max, Toby and Julia crept up on it. Then the fox shook. Its fur turned to black wings! "Caw!" It was a bird, and it shot up past the treetops.
pages.picture: by the woodland pond: the fox changing into a black bird in a swirl of pink, green and blue glints, wings opening and lifting off; Max, Toby and Julia crouched close, gasping

pages.text: "Whoa," said Max. Julia did not say a thing. She was thinking. A fox can not turn into a bird. But a fox that shines pink and green and blue... "That was not a fox," said Julia.
pages.picture: Julia standing by the pond, thinking hard, looking up at the black bird far away in the sky; Max and Toby beside her with open mouths

pages.text: That night, they all sat down to eat. Julia stood up with her Dragon Book. "Mom, Dad, look," she said. In the book was a fox, then a black bird, then a big "?"
pages.picture: evening, the family kitchen table: Mom and Dad at dinner, Max at the table too; Julia standing, holding up her Dragon Book open to her crayon drawing of a fox, an arrow, a black bird and a big question mark; Toby's head peeking in at the open back door

pages.text: Max jumped up on his chair. "It was a fox! Then it was a bird! Then I shot up to the treetops! Then the bird was a fox!" "No, it was not," said Julia. "Max, sit," said Mom. Dad smiled.
pages.picture: Max standing on his chair at the table, waving his arms, telling the story far too loudly; Julia with her hand on her forehead; Mom pointing at his chair; Dad trying not to laugh; Toby at the back door bobbing up and down with glee

pages.text: Then Mom said, "A kid starts in your class in the morning, Julia. He just got here." Julia looked down at her Dragon Book. At the black bird.
pages.picture: close on Julia at the table looking down at her Dragon Book drawing of the black bird, thoughtful; Mom soft behind her; outside the dark window, a black bird sits on the fence in the dusk
